:::{#exr-normal-equations-vector}
#### Normal equations in vector notation

Define the matrix and vector

$$
A \eqdef \sumin \soprod{\vxi},
\qquad
\v{c} \eqdef \sumin \vxi y_i.
$$

Using @exr-rss-gradient-vector,
show that the [normal equations](#def-normal-equations)
can be written as $A \vcoef = \v{c}$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::::{.solution}

Distribute the sum in the gradient from @exr-rss-gradient-vector:

$$
\deriv{\vcoef} \text{RSS}(\vcoef)
= -2 \paren{\sumin \vxi y_i - \sumin \vxi \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}}.
$$

The first sum is $\v{c}$.
The second sum is $A \vcoef$,
because each of its terms regroups as a matrix times $\vcoef$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vxi \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}
&= \vxi \paren{\tprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}
&& \text{(dot product as a transpose product)}\\
&= \paren{\soprod{\vxi}} \vcoef
&& \text{(matrix multiplication is associative)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So the gradient is

$$
\deriv{\vcoef} \text{RSS}(\vcoef) = -2 \paren{\v{c} - A \vcoef}.
$$

The normal equations set this gradient equal to $\vzero$.
Dividing by $-2$ and moving $A \vcoef$ to the other side:

$$
A \vcoef = \v{c}.
$$

::::
